requirements.title: Spec-anchored post-v19 authority
requirements.requirement: Register the approved alignment scope, current authority, requirement mapping, and active-step ledger before behavior changes. Preserve the NIP as wire authority until explicit versioned change control updates it.
requirements.acceptance: New authority, plan adoption, authority validator and current status agree; no undocumented requirement invention.

requirements.title: Immutable historical evidence
requirements.requirement: Preserve v18/v19 frozen requirements, fixtures, reports, private attestations, and T/E/A history. New evidence has new identities and a recorded parent baseline.
requirements.acceptance: Historical hashes and baseline validation remain reproducible against their owning commits; no regenerated historical receipt claims new results.

requirements.title: One independently good commit per step
requirements.requirement: Execute the sequence in order, with one active step, code plus tests together, full diff self-review, and an accurate step report before the next step.
requirements.acceptance: Every completed step has commit SHA, exact commands/results, deviations, and next-step safety; no new failing checks are waved through.

requirements.title: Public/private and orchestration boundaries
requirements.requirement: Keep private TypeScript source, operator paths and raw logs private; use public neutral runner contracts and opaque evidence. Keep gate logic in the public repo and orchestration external.
requirements.acceptance: Repository policy passes; no GitHub-hosted workflows, .act directory, private source, secrets or unauthorized remote mutation.

requirements.title: Accepted-ancestor authoring resume
requirements.requirement: Allow a retained local change to be an accepted ancestor rather than requiring it to remain a current head; reject genuinely missing or incompatible history.
requirements.acceptance: Public A-to-B-to-A, merge, persistence and pruned-history tests prove correct resume and explicit stale failures.

requirements.title: Authoritative actor sequence and operation state
requirements.requirement: Validate restore state against accepted Automerge history; derive durable state from actual encoded change semantics and causal operation maxima. Reject noninitial state on an empty document.
requirements.acceptance: Encoded actor/sequence/start_op/op-count and returned durable counters agree for new actors, multi-operation changes, remote descendants and empty merges; failures are atomic.

requirements.title: Evaluator-to-authoring bridge
requirements.requirement: Expose a public, safe route from a complete accepted report to subsequent local authoring, bound to coordinate, revision, control/history and validated actor state. Keep upstream mutable Automerge types private.
requirements.acceptance: Two public-API devices can evaluate remote history, resume, edit again and converge; incomplete, mismatched and stale reports cannot become authoritative authoring input.

requirements.title: General semantic editing
requirements.requirement: Extend authoring beyond the four root-only constructors to existing/nested map and list operations, deletion, UTF-16 text editing, counter increments and marks, within supported protocol semantics.
requirements.acceptance: Each supported family has positive, concurrent, invalid-input and atomic-failure tests; no direct upstream Automerge dependency is required in consumer examples.

requirements.title: Bounded frontier fan-in
requirements.requirement: Support large frontiers through a bounded deterministic sequence of valid empty merge changes without raising sealed per-change or control limits.
requirements.acceptance: Boundary tests include 64/65/256/257 and larger valid frontiers; each chunk obeys dependency limits and state/counter rules; cancellation/failure leaves resumable durable intent.

requirements.title: Control authoring matches protocol
requirements.requirement: Reconcile the public control constructor with existing genesis, predecessor, terminal/freeze and successor clauses before lifecycle examples depend on it.
requirements.acceptance: Reproduced constructor inconsistencies have focused tests and author-then-validate/evaluate coverage; newly discovered details are separately recorded from the original review.

requirements.title: Bounded public missing-evidence hints
requirements.requirement: Expose sufficient typed coordinate/revision-bound missing-reference information for dependency recovery, distinguishing missing EventId/control references from missing ChangeHash dependencies without companion access to private Automerge internals.
requirements.acceptance: Public-only recovery tests can discover the actual missing references, query/reingest sufficient evidence and complete evaluation; foreign-coordinate hints, unbounded output and false complete hints are rejected or bounded explicitly.

requirements.title: Complete checkpoint save framing
requirements.requirement: Require a structurally complete Automerge save for the checkpoint profile before generic loading; reject change chunks, incremental streams, concatenated/trailing payloads as required by the profile.
requirements.acceptance: Correctly signed descriptor/chunk fixtures distinguish full saves from raw changes despite valid commitments; do not use cross-language reserialization-byte equality as validity.

requirements.title: Hostile candidate isolation
requirements.requirement: Preserve a sufficient valid checkpoint chunk set when an unrelated unauthorized extra carrier is added, under an explicit normative candidate-selection decision.
requirements.acceptance: Versioned rules and signed differential vectors precede code; invalid carrier outcomes remain visible while valid checkpoint availability is preserved.

requirements.title: Bounded and truthful work
requirements.requirement: Preserve checked arithmetic, bounded allocation, iterative graph handling and deterministic incomplete/cancelled outcomes; test bulk upstream decode work at process level.
requirements.acceptance: No panic or partial document is presented as complete; targeted budget boundaries, bounded queues and process RSS/CPU evidence cover changed paths.

requirements.title: Explicit compatibility and migration
requirements.requirement: Keep revisions/limits sealed and signed strings stable. Classify each correction as API-only, existing-rule repair or normative change, and apply the NIP version/successor rules.
requirements.acceptance: Old/new behavior matrix, new evidence identities, API migration notes and independent differential results exist for affected semantics.

requirements.title: Companion boundary
requirements.requirement: Implement native networking, async coordination, persistence, signing and outbox in companion package(s) outside nostr_automerge; preserve the deterministic batch oracle.
requirements.acceptance: Core dependency graph and public API remain free of networking/storage/runtime/FFI; companion communicates through semantic core types.

requirements.title: Real local relay round trip
requirements.requirement: Provide signed publish, subscription/discovery, bounded backfill/live ingestion and explicit acknowledgements/readback against a pinned local relay.
requirements.acceptance: Two independent processes exchange events and assert exact semantic state, selected control, heads and completion; no public relay is required for deterministic tests.

requirements.title: Immutable evidence and rebuildable projections
requirements.requirement: Persist signed evidence and provenance separately from caches/projections; maintain a durable actor record and transactionally consistent metadata.
requirements.acceptance: Restart/rebuild from evidence returns the same complete reference outcome; corrupted or incompatible caches cannot bypass core validation.

requirements.title: Atomic durable outbox
requirements.requirement: Atomically retain next actor state, exact signed carriers and outbox intent before publish; serialize/fence competing authors; recover uncertainty by retrying the same EventId.
requirements.acceptance: Crash matrix, concurrent writers, lost acknowledgements and restart tests show no lost authored event, duplicate actor sequence or accidental re-sign/re-author identity drift.

requirements.title: Bounded multi-relay recovery
requirements.requirement: Handle omissions, duplication, reorder, disconnect, missing dependencies and slow relays with bounded queues and retries; transport timing never changes core consensus.
requirements.acceptance: Fault-injected multi-relay tests converge when sufficient evidence arrives; incomplete evidence stays explicitly incomplete; cancellation preserves pending intent.

requirements.title: Backup and restore
requirements.requirement: Export/import immutable signed history and the documented local recovery state with integrity/version checks and safe actor ownership handling.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh-process restore reproduces history/heads/digest; snapshot alone is not trusted history; stale/cloned actor restores cannot silently reuse an actor sequence.

requirements.title: Signer and secret boundary
requirements.requirement: Keep key custody outside core, sign exact prepared event identity, validate returned signature/public key, and default to content/secret-safe diagnostics.
requirements.acceptance: Wrong-key/invalid-signature/cancel/error tests fail without publishing; persisted signed bytes are reused; normal logs contain no raw contents or secret keys.

requirements.title: Complete canonical example catalog
requirements.requirement: Maintain the approved 14 core, four native integration and one interop scenario with one discoverable catalog and learning path.
requirements.acceptance: All 19 directory contracts in EXAMPLES_CATALOG.md exist, are mapped to requirements and have working documented commands.

requirements.title: Executable semantic examples
requirements.requirement: Execute example bodies with assertions and timeouts/cleanup where applicable; all-targets compilation alone is insufficient.
requirements.acceptance: Catalog runner executes every required example in its declared lane; key values/heads/control/completion/errors are asserted, including packaged quickstarts.

requirements.title: Priority six learning path
requirements.requirement: Make signed round trip, authoring resume, concurrent offline merge, dependency recovery, relay round trip and durable outbox the first coherent adoption path.
requirements.acceptance: A new contributor can follow these six using public APIs and local tools; each points to prerequisites, expected output and relevant failure cases.

requirements.title: Portable assurance execution
requirements.requirement: Remove undeclared cargo extbuild as a required default for current reruns; keep optional operator wrapping explicit and versioned.
requirements.acceptance: Clean documented environment runs current lanes without private tools; wrapper argv/exit/error tests pass; historical receipts remain immutable.

requirements.title: Real independent interop and negative comparator
requirements.requirement: Use the selected current neutral distribution, two processes/eight delivery orders as applicable, and an actual deliberately mismatched comparison that must fail.
requirements.acceptance: Rust repeatability and independent-runner agreement are separately recorded; comparator negative test executes the real comparison path and stale manifests cannot be silently chosen.

requirements.title: Package self-containment and licensing
requirements.requirement: Include required package-local test assets or isolate repository-only tests; include MIT and Apache-2.0 license texts and verify extracted archives and consumer use.
requirements.acceptance: cargo package, extracted archive checks/tests and minimal consumer/examples pass without ancestor checkout files; archive license and fixture inventory is verified.

requirements.title: MSRV, features and platform truth
requirements.requirement: Continuously verify Rust 1.99.0 development toolchain and declared MSRV, supported feature combinations and actual native platforms; make only tested claims.
requirements.acceptance: Documented supported matrix is green; unsupported WASM/browser and unrun platforms are explicitly unclaimed, not silently advertised.

requirements.title: Meaningful robustness and independent assurance
requirements.requirement: Run sustained fuzzing, targeted property/mutation checks, process resource/load and supply-chain checks; obtain independent review/interop evidence or retain explicit qualification blocks.
requirements.acceptance: Recorded durations/seeds/build identities/findings and closure exist; compiling fuzz targets or validating old receipts is never reported as a new campaign.

requirements.title: Truthful current documentation
requirements.requirement: Replace stale navigation/status with a current scope page and accurate API/quickstart/contribution/testing/migration docs while preserving historical artifacts.
requirements.acceptance: Current docs point to the alignment plan and real commands; no completed v19 work is presented as an active RCLD141 task or future-only interop claim.

requirements.title: Readiness separated from publication
requirements.requirement: Prepare a verifiable local release candidate and hold ledger without publishing, tagging, deploying or changing remote repositories.
requirements.acceptance: Code-completion and assurance status are distinct; external assurance/event allocation/NIP submission/production/release/publication/deployment holds are accurately recorded and only separately authorized actions are performed.
